blocks.text:
Breakfast. Then we will head towards the smaller but equally beautiful lagoons – Honda, Chiar Kkota, Hedionda, Cañapa, and a stop at the viewpoint of Volcán Ollagüe. The volcano is still active, and smoke billows from its crater, offering a majestic sight. Next, your journey will take you to the Chiguana salt flats, which stand out from others due to their large deposits of sodium and potassium nitrate, making these salt flats particularly unique.

Finally, you will visit the largest dried-up salt lake on Earth – Salar de Uyuni. The lake is located in the southern part of Bolivia on a high plateau at an altitude of 3650 meters. Its total area is about 11,000 square kilometers. In the center of the lake, the salt crust reaches a thickness of 10 meters. During the dry season, the lake is a vast salt desert. The salt reserves here are estimated at around 10 billion tons. During the rainy season, the lake is covered with a thin layer of water, which does not hinder travel across Salar de Uyuni by jeep. During the rainy season, the salt flat becomes the world's largest mirror.

On the way to the Great Salt Valley of Uyuni, you will see how salt is extracted and processed in the town of Colchani. After this, you will visit a place called "Eyes of Water," where you can observe geological formations of the local landscape and watch the salt processing process. Then, on Fish Island, you will see several giant cacti and enjoy the view of the salt valley. Lunch (boxed lunch) is included.

At the end of the tour, transfer to Uyuni.
